newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: OLYMPIC PVC PLASTICS TUSSLE
The Olympic Co-ordination Authority says it's using PVC plastics for underground telephone and electrical wiring, because it's more suitable and comes at a competitive price.

Greenpeace protestors today exposed large amounts of Poly Vinyl Chloride piping on the Homebush site and replaced some of it with what they claim is more environmentally friendly piping. The environment manager for the Authority, Doctor Colin Grant, says the Authority has minimised the use of PVC plastics at the Olympic site, in accordance with the green games bid.
But Doctor Grant says PVC has a particular property which is useful in regard to fire.
MAYOR DESCRIBES MIXED RACE CHILDREN AS MONGRELS
The Ethnic Communities Council says the Port Lincoln Mayor, Peter Davis has described children of mixed race marriages as mongrels.
Council chairman, Victor Rebikoff says the Council has had complaints about Councillor Davis, and says he should be sacked over his official support of controversial MP Pauline Hanson.
Nine out of the ten Port Lincoln councillors resigned in protest after the Mayor used Council letterhead in a statement of support for Ms Hanson's views on immigration and multiculturalism.
Mr Rebikoff has told ABC radio that he'll call on South Australian Premier Dean Brown to sack Mr Davis, and will be taking the complaints to the Race Discrimination Commission.
DEATH IN CUSTODY
Queensland's Corrective Services Commission says a 31-year-old Aboriginal woman has died at the Townsville Prison in north Queensland.
A spokesman for the Commission says the woman from Doomadgee was found dead in her cell at 7-30 this morning.
Investigations are continuing, but the spokesman says the woman appears to have died from natural causes.
BLACKHAWK INQUIRY RESUMES
At the military inquiry into the June Blackhawk helicopter disaster in Townville, the co-pilot of Blackhawk five on the night of the crash has resumed giving evidence.
Captain Scott Bedbow says the flying formation used on the night of the crash has been limited since the accident, to counter-terrorist exercises only.
Captain Benbow has also told the inquiry that his profession was highly demanding, saying that at times unreasonable requests were made.
He said it was up to the squadron to say whether those requests could be met.
When asked about the pressure of the job and why they were subjected to it, he said it was because they were training for war.
NT LEADS IN RENEWABLE ENERGY
A conference in Darwin has heard that the Northern Territory is leading the country in the use of solar hot water systems.
The international conference on solar energy has opened this morning ahead of the weekend's start of the World Solar Challenge, from Darwin to Adelaide.
Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone told delegates experience with providing alternative energy in remote areas is also being exported from the Territory.
TASMANIA'S UPPER HOUSE CHALLENGED
In Tasmania, the legality of the state's Upper House has been challenged, raising questions of whether any legislation it's passed since September, including the budget, is valid.
This follows the deadlock on electoral boundaries in the house.
Member for Newdegate Ross Ginn has asked the State Government to clarify the legal standing of the House following advice from a constitutional lawyer.
Mr Ginn says fellow MLC, Doug Parkinson told parliament last night he's been advised that 19 seats in the upper House are legally vacant.
Tasmania's Upper House has been without electoral boundaries since July because Labor and the Greens in the House of Assembly have blocked the necessary legislation.
CHILD PORNOGRAPHY CATALOGUES SENT AROUND THE COUNTRY
Australian Federal Police believe child pornography catalogues down loaded on the internet, were sent out randomly all around Australia.
Seven local users contacted police after they received personalised mail, offering them various types of child pornography.
The AFP says the distribution of the catalogues appears to be part of a fraud scam.
Sydney businessman Brian Parker says he received the e-mail message two days ago, which offered a range of child pornographic material, and had a New York address.

Meanwhile, head of the AFP's Regional Investigation Team Brian Hepworth, says a joint investigation with United States authorities has lead to the detainment of a man New York Police believe is involved in the scam.
YOTHU YINDI SUPPORTING HOLLOWS FOUNDATION
The band Yothu Yindi is teaming up with the Fred Hollows Foundation to spread the message about the organisation's work in Africa.
Lead singer Mandawuy Yunupingo is meeting African leaders later this month, and performing in Zimbabwe and South Africa.
A highlight is a concert in Johannesburg with Bjork, Tracey Chapman and the Spindoctors.
